lines.text: A little ring rolls all the way around the inside of a big hoop.
lines.caption: A little ring rolls all the way around the inside of a big hoop.

lines.text: How many times does it turn? Lots of people guess five. <short pause> But it's NOT five!
lines.caption: How many times does it turn? Lots of people guess five. But it's NOT five!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's count the turns together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's count the turns together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: A small ring with a radius of two rolls around the inside of a large hoop.
lines.caption: A small ring with a radius of two rolls around the inside of a large hoop.

lines.text: The large hoop's radius is ten.
lines.caption: The large hoop's radius is ten.

lines.text: It rolls without slipping, always touching, until it's back where it started.
lines.caption: It rolls without slipping, always touching, until it's back where it started.

lines.text: How many full turns does the small ring make?
lines.caption: How many full turns does the small ring make?

lines.text: Is it three, four, five, six, or eight?
lines.caption: Is it three, four, five, six, or eight?

lines.text: So what do we know?
lines.caption: So what do we know?

lines.text: The ring has a radius of two, and the hoop has a radius of ten.
lines.caption: The ring has a radius of two, and the hoop has a radius of ten.

lines.text: No slipping means it rolls like a bike tire on a road. It never skids.
lines.caption: No slipping means it rolls like a bike tire on a road. It never skids.

lines.text: Now, what is a full turn? Let's draw an arrow on the ring.
lines.caption: Now, what is a full turn? Let's draw an arrow on the ring.

lines.text: One full turn means the arrow points the same way again.
lines.caption: One full turn means the arrow points the same way again.

lines.text: Our job is to count how many times that happens in one trip around.
lines.caption: Our job is to count how many times that happens in one trip around.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's start with something simpler: a ring rolling on a flat floor.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's start with something simpler: a ring rolling on a flat floor.

lines.text: Watch the arrow. After one full turn, it points straight down again.
lines.caption: Watch the arrow. After one full turn, it points straight down again.

lines.text: How far did the center move? Exactly one rim length, laid flat on the floor.
lines.caption: How far did the center move? Exactly one rim length, laid flat on the floor.

lines.text: The ring's rim is two times pi times two. That's four pi.
lines.caption: The ring's rim is two times pi times two. That's four pi.

lines.text: So here's our rule. Each full turn moves the center one rim length.
lines.caption: So here's our rule. Each full turn moves the center one rim length.

lines.text: This rule still works on a curved track, as long as nothing slips.
lines.caption: This rule still works on a curved track, as long as nothing slips.

lines.text: Now back to the hoop. Where does the center of the ring go?
lines.caption: Now back to the hoop. Where does the center of the ring go?

lines.text: The ring always touches the hoop, so its center always stays a distance of two from it.
lines.caption: The ring always touches the hoop, so its center always stays a distance of two from it.

lines.text: So the center goes around a smaller circle, with radius ten minus two. That's eight.
lines.caption: So the center goes around a smaller circle, with radius ten minus two. That's eight.

lines.text: That circle is two times pi times eight long. That's sixteen pi.
lines.caption: That circle is two times pi times eight long. That's sixteen pi.

lines.text: Each turn moves the center four pi.
lines.caption: Each turn moves the center four pi.

lines.text: So sixteen pi over four pi gives four. The answer is four full turns. That's B!
lines.caption: So sixteen pi over four pi gives four. The answer is four full turns. That's B!

lines.text: Let's watch it roll, to be sure.
lines.caption: Let's watch it roll, to be sure.

lines.text: Count each time the arrow points straight down again.
lines.caption: Count each time the arrow points straight down again.

lines.text: Notice that the center goes counterclockwise, but the ring spins clockwise.
lines.caption: Notice that the center goes counterclockwise, but the ring spins clockwise.

lines.text: Keep counting, all the way back to the start.
lines.caption: Keep counting, all the way back to the start.

lines.text: Four full turns, just like we worked out!
lines.caption: Four full turns, just like we worked out!

lines.text: Here's another way. It also explains why five is so tempting.
lines.caption: Here's another way. It also explains why five is so tempting.

lines.text: Now watch the red dot at the tip of the arrow.
lines.caption: Now watch the red dot at the tip of the arrow.

lines.text: Each time the dot touches the hoop, we leave a mark.
lines.caption: Each time the dot touches the hoop, we leave a mark.

lines.text: Five marks! The hoop's rim is twenty pi, and the ring's rim is four pi.
lines.caption: Five marks! The hoop's rim is twenty pi, and the ring's rim is four pi.

lines.text: Twenty pi over four pi is five. So the dot touches the hoop five times.
lines.caption: Twenty pi over four pi is five. So the dot touches the hoop five times.

lines.text: But the arrow only pointed down again four times. Where did one turn go?
lines.caption: But the arrow only pointed down again four times. Where did one turn go?

lines.text: Let's try a silly experiment. Glue the ring so it can't roll, and slide it around.
lines.caption: Let's try a silly experiment. Glue the ring so it can't roll, and slide it around.

lines.text: The dot always touches the hoop. Now watch the arrow.
lines.caption: The dot always touches the hoop. Now watch the arrow.

lines.text: Even with no rolling, the arrow turns once, the same way the center goes.
lines.caption: Even with no rolling, the arrow turns once, the same way the center goes.

lines.text: So the trip around the loop turns the ring once, counterclockwise.
lines.caption: So the trip around the loop turns the ring once, counterclockwise.

lines.text: Now let's roll it again, with the glued ring drawn on top.
lines.caption: Now let's roll it again, with the glued ring drawn on top.

lines.text: The glued ring's dot always faces the hoop. The rolling dot comes back to the hoop five times.
lines.caption: The glued ring's dot always faces the hoop. The rolling dot comes back to the hoop five times.

lines.text: That's five turns clockwise, counted from the side of the hoop.
lines.caption: That's five turns clockwise, counted from the side of the hoop.

lines.text: The loop's turn goes the opposite way, so it cancels one. Five minus one is four!
lines.caption: The loop's turn goes the opposite way, so it cancels one. Five minus one is four!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? It's a fast check, and it shows why five is a trap.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? It's a fast check, and it shows why five is a trap.

lines.text: Now let's look at the traps.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the traps.

lines.text: Five uses the hoop's whole rim. It forgets the one turn the loop takes back.
lines.caption: Five uses the hoop's whole rim. It forgets the one turn the loop takes back.

lines.text: Then there's eight. It uses two pi for the ring's rim. That's the rim for a radius of one.
lines.caption: Then there's eight. It uses two pi for the ring's rim. That's the rim for a radius of one.

lines.text: Six is what you'd get rolling around the OUTSIDE of the hoop. There, the loop adds a turn.
lines.caption: Six is what you'd get rolling around the OUTSIDE of the hoop. There, the loop adds a turn.

lines.text: Three takes away the ring's whole width. That makes the center's path radius six, not eight.
lines.caption: Three takes away the ring's whole width. That makes the center's path radius six, not eight.

lines.text: Only four survives. That's B!
lines.caption: Only four survives. That's B!

lines.text: Your turn! Here's a twist.
lines.caption: Your turn! Here's a twist.

lines.text: A coin with a radius of three rolls around the OUTSIDE of a plate.
lines.caption: A coin with a radius of three rolls around the OUTSIDE of a plate.

lines.text: The plate has a radius of twelve.
lines.caption: The plate has a radius of twelve.

lines.text: How many full turns does the coin make on one trip around?
lines.caption: How many full turns does the coin make on one trip around?

lines.text: Here's a hint: follow the center!
lines.caption: Here's a hint: follow the center!

lines.text: Pause the video and try it. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Pause the video and try it. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Outside, the center stays a distance of three from the plate.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Outside, the center stays a distance of three from the plate.

lines.text: So its path has a radius of twelve plus three. That's fifteen.
lines.caption: So its path has a radius of twelve plus three. That's fifteen.

lines.text: The path is thirty pi long. Each turn moves the center six pi.
lines.caption: The path is thirty pi long. Each turn moves the center six pi.

lines.text: Thirty pi over six pi is five. So the coin makes five full turns!
lines.caption: Thirty pi over six pi is five. So the coin makes five full turns!

lines.text: Let's check it the other way. Twelve over three is four, and the loop adds one.
lines.caption: Let's check it the other way. Twelve over three is four, and the loop adds one.

lines.text: That's five again! Outside, the coin spins the SAME way it travels.
lines.caption: That's five again! Outside, the coin spins the SAME way it travels.

lines.text: Great work!
lines.caption: Great work!

lines.text: So here's the big idea.
lines.caption: So here's the big idea.

lines.text: To count turns, follow the center. Each turn moves it one rim length.
lines.caption: To count turns, follow the center. Each turn moves it one rim length.

lines.text: For the path of the center, take away the ring's radius inside a hoop. Add it outside.
lines.caption: For the path of the center, take away the ring's radius inside a hoop. Add it outside.

lines.text: Thanks for rolling along with me! I'm Vantee. See you next time, and keep exploring!
lines.caption: Thanks for rolling along with me! I'm Vantee. See you next time, and keep exploring!
